fields.label: Voyage under SOLAS I/2(d)
fields.help: The voyage must run between a country to which SOLAS applies and a port outside that country, in either direction.

fields.label: Does a listed SOLAS vessel exception describe the ship?
fields.help: Rule I/3(a) lists these categories. The separate cargo-ship tonnage test is evaluated independently. Other SOLAS chapters can expressly apply.

fields.label: Sailing solely within the I/3(b) Great Lakes–St Lawrence boundary
fields.help: Use the line from Cap des Rosiers to West Point on Anticosti Island and the 63rd meridian north of the island. Chapter V has its own provisions.

fields.label: Passengers counted under SOLAS I/2(e)
fields.help: Exclude the master, crew, persons working on the ship's business and children under one year of age. More than 12 makes a passenger ship for this definition.

fields.label: Ship's gross tonnage for this SOLAS threshold
fields.help: Use the tonnage applicable to SOLAS on the ship's official records for the date in question. Historical tonnage treatment can differ. This is a tonnage measure, distinct from deadweight.

sections.title: International voyage and chapter-specific application
sections.text:
Regulation 1. APPLICATION
(a) Unless expressly provided otherwise, the present Regulations apply only to ships engaged on international voyages.
(b) The classes of ships to which each Chapter applies are more precisely defined, and the extent of the application is shown, in each Chapter.

all.source: SOLAS article II and the IMO depositary state or territorial action

sections.caveat: These are Chapter I's general application rules. Each chapter specifies its own coverage. Chapter V and the polar provisions of Chapter XIV can reach vessels outside the general rule.

sections.title: Ships entitled to fly the flag of a contracting state
sections.text: Article II. APPLICATION The present Convention shall apply to ships entitled to fly the flag of States the Governments of which are Contracting Governments.

all.source: SOLAS article II and the IMO depositary state or territorial action

sections.caveat: Article II uses entitlement to fly a contracting government's flag.

sections.title: Definition of an international voyage
sections.text: (d) "International voyage" means a voyage from a country to which the present Convention applies to a port outside such country, or conversely.

all.source: SOLAS article II and the IMO depositary state or territorial action

sections.caveat: Read the country-to-port definition in both directions.

sections.title: Who counts as a passenger, passenger ships and cargo ships
sections.text:
(e) A passenger is every person other than:
(i) The master and the members of the crew or other persons employed or engaged in any capacity on board a ship on the business of that ship; and
(ii) A child under one year of age.
(f) A passenger ship is a ship which carries more than twelve passengers.
(g) A cargo ship is any ship which is not a passenger ship.

all.source: SOLAS article II and the IMO depositary state or territorial action

sections.caveat: Use the treaty passenger count. Any ship outside the passenger-ship definition is a cargo ship for this purpose.

sections.title: Excluded vessels, cargo-ship tonnage and the Great Lakes boundary

all.source: SOLAS article II and the IMO depositary state or territorial action

sections.caveat: These are Chapter I's general application rules. Each chapter specifies its own coverage. Chapter V and the polar provisions of Chapter XIV can reach vessels outside the general rule.

sections.title: Administrative exemption for a single exceptional international voyage
sections.text:
Regulation 4. EXEMPTIONS
(a) A ship which is not normally engaged on international voyages but which, in exceptional circumstances, is required to undertake a single international voyage may be exempted by the Administration from any of the requirements of the present Regulations provided that it complies with safety requirements which are adequate in the opinion of the Administration for the voyage which is to be undertaken by the ship.

all.source: SOLAS article II and the IMO depositary state or territorial action

sections.caveat: Only the Administration may grant this exemption, subject to adequate safety requirements for the voyage. Check the decision and its terms.

sections.title: International voyage and chapter-specific application
sections.text:
Regulation 1. APPLICATION
(a) Unless expressly provided otherwise, the present Regulations apply only to ships engaged on international voyages.
(b) The classes of ships to which each Chapter applies are more precisely defined, and the extent of the application is shown, in each Chapter.

all.source: SOLAS article II and the IMO depositary state or territorial action

sections.caveat: These are Chapter I's general application rules. Each chapter specifies its own coverage. Chapter V and the polar provisions of Chapter XIV can reach vessels outside the general rule.

sections.title: Ships entitled to fly the flag of a contracting state
sections.text: Article II. APPLICATION The present Convention shall apply to ships entitled to fly the flag of States the Governments of which are Contracting Governments.

all.source: SOLAS article II and the IMO depositary state or territorial action

sections.caveat: Article II uses entitlement to fly a contracting government's flag.

sections.title: Definition of an international voyage
sections.text: (d) "International voyage" means a voyage from a country to which the present Convention applies to a port outside such country, or conversely.

all.source: SOLAS article II and the IMO depositary state or territorial action

sections.caveat: Read the country-to-port definition in both directions.

sections.title: Who counts as a passenger, passenger ships and cargo ships
sections.text:
(e) A passenger is every person other than:
(i) The master and the members of the crew or other persons employed or engaged in any capacity on board a ship on the business of that ship; and
(ii) A child under one year of age.
(f) A passenger ship is a ship which carries more than twelve passengers.
(g) A cargo ship is any ship which is not a passenger ship.

all.source: SOLAS article II and the IMO depositary state or territorial action

sections.caveat: Use the treaty passenger count. Any ship outside the passenger-ship definition is a cargo ship for this purpose.

sections.title: Excluded vessels, cargo-ship tonnage and the Great Lakes boundary

all.source: SOLAS article II and the IMO depositary state or territorial action

sections.caveat: These are Chapter I's general application rules. Each chapter specifies its own coverage. Chapter V and the polar provisions of Chapter XIV can reach vessels outside the general rule.

sections.title: Administrative exemption for a single exceptional international voyage
sections.text:
Regulation 4. EXEMPTIONS
(a) A ship which is not normally engaged on international voyages but which, in exceptional circumstances, is required to undertake a single international voyage may be exempted by the Administration from any of the requirements of the present Regulations provided that it complies with safety requirements which are adequate in the opinion of the Administration for the voyage which is to be undertaken by the ship.

all.source: SOLAS article II and the IMO depositary state or territorial action

sections.caveat: Only the Administration may grant this exemption, subject to adequate safety requirements for the voyage. Check the decision and its terms.

(a) Unless expressly provided otherwise, the present Regulations apply only to ships engaged on international voyages.
(b) The classes of ships to which each Chapter applies are more precisely defined, and the extent of the application is shown, in each Chapter.

sections.title: Who counts as a passenger, passenger ships and cargo ships
sections.text:

(i) The master and the members of the crew or other persons employed or engaged in any capacity on board a ship on the business of that ship; and
(ii) A child under one year of age.

(g) A cargo ship is any ship which is not a passenger ship.

all.source: SOLAS article II and the IMO depositary state or territorial action

sections.caveat: Use the treaty passenger count. Any ship outside the passenger-ship definition is a cargo ship for this purpose.

versions.label: SOLAS general provisions · Naoero
versions.kind: Original treaty, selected provisions checked against later editions

flagEvidence.register: IMO Status Book 2026, volume I, SOLAS 1974

sections.title: International voyage and chapter-specific application
sections.text:
Regulation 1. APPLICATION
(a) Unless expressly provided otherwise, the present Regulations apply only to ships engaged on international voyages.
(b) The classes of ships to which each Chapter applies are more precisely defined, and the extent of the application is shown, in each Chapter.

all.source: SOLAS article II and the IMO depositary state or territorial action

sections.caveat: These are Chapter I's general application rules. Each chapter specifies its own coverage. Chapter V and the polar provisions of Chapter XIV can reach vessels outside the general rule.

sections.title: Ships entitled to fly the flag of a contracting state
sections.text: Article II. APPLICATION The present Convention shall apply to ships entitled to fly the flag of States the Governments of which are Contracting Governments.

all.source: SOLAS article II and the IMO depositary state or territorial action

sections.caveat: Article II uses entitlement to fly a contracting government's flag.

sections.title: Definition of an international voyage
sections.text: (d) "International voyage" means a voyage from a country to which the present Convention applies to a port outside such country, or conversely.

all.source: SOLAS article II and the IMO depositary state or territorial action

sections.caveat: Read the country-to-port definition in both directions.

sections.title: Who counts as a passenger, passenger ships and cargo ships
sections.text:
(e) A passenger is every person other than:
(i) The master and the members of the crew or other persons employed or engaged in any capacity on board a ship on the business of that ship; and
(ii) A child under one year of age.
(f) A passenger ship is a ship which carries more than twelve passengers.
(g) A cargo ship is any ship which is not a passenger ship.

all.source: SOLAS article II and the IMO depositary state or territorial action

sections.caveat: Use the treaty passenger count. Any ship outside the passenger-ship definition is a cargo ship for this purpose.

sections.title: Excluded vessels, cargo-ship tonnage and the Great Lakes boundary

all.source: SOLAS article II and the IMO depositary state or territorial action

sections.caveat: These are Chapter I's general application rules. Each chapter specifies its own coverage. Chapter V and the polar provisions of Chapter XIV can reach vessels outside the general rule.

sections.title: Administrative exemption for a single exceptional international voyage
sections.text:
Regulation 4. EXEMPTIONS
(a) A ship which is not normally engaged on international voyages but which, in exceptional circumstances, is required to undertake a single international voyage may be exempted by the Administration from any of the requirements of the present Regulations provided that it complies with safety requirements which are adequate in the opinion of the Administration for the voyage which is to be undertaken by the ship.

all.source: SOLAS article II and the IMO depositary state or territorial action

sections.caveat: Only the Administration may grant this exemption, subject to adequate safety requirements for the voyage. Check the decision and its terms.
